requirement: Cryptographic initialization vector manager for AES-CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC (HMAC-SHA256), strictly enforcing cryptographically random 16-byte IVs per encryption, constant-time MAC verification, and preventing IV reuse or predictable sequences.
skeleton: SecureCBCEncryptor class with encrypt and decrypt methods using cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers and hmac.
caption: A cryptography AES-CBC encryptor that pairs an unpredictable random IV per message with Encrypt-then-MAC authentication. BLOCK_SIZE_BYTES is 16 and KEY_SIZE_BYTES is 32. SecureCBCEncryptor takes separate encryption and MAC keys and raises ValueError when either is not exactly 32 bytes. encrypt(plaintext) raises TypeError when the plaintext is not bytes, draws a fresh 16-byte IV from secrets.token_bytes for every call rather than using a counter, a timestamp, a padded short value, or one IV fixed at construction, pads the plaintext with PKCS7 to the 128-bit block size, and encrypts it with AES in CBC mode under that IV. It then computes an HMAC-SHA256 tag over the IV concatenated with the ciphertext and returns the ciphertext, IV, and 32-byte tag. decrypt(ciphertext, iv, mac) raises ValueError when the IV is not exactly 16 bytes, recomputes the tag over IV and ciphertext, and compares it with hmac.compare_digest in constant time, raising ValueError reporting that message authentication failed before any decryption happens, so tampered data never reaches the padding logic. Only after a valid tag does it decrypt and strip the PKCS7 padding. The fixture asserts a 16-byte IV, a 32-byte tag, and a correct round trip, that five encryptions produce five distinct IVs whose values are not consecutive and are not mostly zero bytes, that a flipped tag byte and a flipped ciphertext byte each raise ValueError reporting Message authentication failed, and that wrong encryption and MAC key lengths raise ValueError with their messages.

rationale.teaches: AES-CBC with a fresh random 16-byte IV per message, Encrypt-then-MAC over IV plus ciphertext, constant-time MAC verification before decryption, and IV length validated.
rationale.why: A predictable IV yields valid ciphertext that decrypts correctly, so a round-trip test passes. The fixture encrypts twice and compares IVs, and tampers with the MAC to check decryption is refused.

candidates.why_wrong: The IV is a counter, so an attacker who sees one IV predicts every later one.
The IV is the current timestamp, so two messages in the same second share an IV and IVs are guessable.
One IV is generated at construction and reused, so every message from the instance shares it.
The MAC check is skipped, so a tampered ciphertext decrypts to garbage without an error.
The IV is 8 random bytes zero-padded to 16, so half of each IV is constant.
